target.title: fix(slack): prevent duplicate reply controls
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Slack users could see the same approval, button, or select row twice when a reply supplied both the canonical portable presentation and its deprecated interactive mirror.

## Why This Change Was Made

Slack now uses one shared merge path for ordinary replies, outbound sends and block budgeting, and message-action sends. It renders deprecated interactive controls after native offsets, then subtracts only exact OpenClaw-generated mirrors as a multiset; raw Slack blocks, intentional repeated presentation rows, surplus legacy rows, and controls with different labels, values, URLs, styles, placeholders, or options remain unchanged.

## User Impact

Mirrored Slack controls render once and keep unique Block Kit IDs. Intentionally repeated or meaningfully different controls still render independently.

## Evidence

- Rewritten exact head: `bfb2495e7f4a0cbe1c41d8db2feb863a2f57a5a0` (one commit on `c5bdd64442b`, with contributor credit preserved).
- Focused proof for the unchanged patch: `run_c4c6e35742ac` — 75/75 tests; `run_605d0989658a` — full `check:changed` passed.
- Regressions cover exact mirrored buttons and selects, authored repeated rows, surplus legacy rows, semantic differences, reconstructed object-key order, message-action sends, final outbound delivery, and the 50-block boundary.
- Fresh autoreview on the rebased head: clean, no accepted or actionable findings.
- `git diff --check` passes; hosted exact-head CI is running.
- Live Slack proof remains required before merge: one visible control row plus a successful button or select interaction.

AI-assisted: the contributor branch was narrowed and rewritten with Codex; contributor credit is preserved.
